Account- Role & Access Administration Fl: Verify the complete end-to-end Administrator journey through the actual UI: dashboard stats accuracy
column6: the Update Account status/role whitelist guards

Account- Role & Access Administration Fl: Admin views Dashboard stats and the figures are real, not fabricated.
column3: 1. Log in as ADMINISTRATOR. 2. Open Admin Dashboard. 3. Cross-check totalUsers/totalRoles/totalCourses/totalEnrollments and the Top 5 Courses list against known recent test data (e.g. courses/enrollments created in SYS_FLOW_ENR).
column4: All figures reflect actual current data (in-memory Java aggregation + a native Top-Courses query), matching what was independently observed in other flows; nothing is a placeholder/mock value.
column5: Admin logged in; recent enrollments/courses exist from earlier flows.

Account- Role & Access Administration Fl: A week with zero real registrations shows a genuine zero on the weekly registration chart, not a fabricated positive number.
column3: 1. Identify (or wait for) a 7-day window with no real new signups. 2. Open the Dashboard's weekly registration chart for that window.
column4: The chart shows 0 for that week - it must not synthesize a fake positive count (previously `totalUsers / 7`-based fabrication, fixed 2026-07-22).
column5: A week with zero real registrations exists or can be observed.
column15: Regression check for the fabricated-dashboard-data bug documented in doc/specs/03-rbac.md Edge Cases.

Account- Role & Access Administration Fl: Admin searches and filters the account list by role type and free text.
column3: 1. Open Admin > Accounts. 2. Filter by roleType=trainer. 3. Enter a search term matching a known user's name/email.
column4: The list narrows to only TRAINER accounts, then further to rows matching the search term; pagination controls reflect the filtered result count.
column5: Multiple accounts with different roles exist.

Account- Role & Access Administration Fl: Requesting a non-existent account's detail returns a proper not-found state, not a generic bad-request error.
column3: 1. Open Admin > Accounts. 2. Navigate to a user detail using an ID that does not exist (e.g. a very large/deleted ID).
column4: The UI shows a clear "user not found" state; the underlying API returns 404 Not Found (not 400 Bad Request).
column5: No account exists with the chosen ID.
column15: Regression check - `GET /api/admin/users/{id}` was fixed 2026-07-22 to return 404 instead of 400 for a missing user.

Account- Role & Access Administration Fl: Admin creates a new account directly with a whitelisted role, and it is immediately usable.
column3: 1. Open Admin > Accounts > Create Account. 2. Fill in email/name/password and select role=TRAINER_LEAD. 3. Save. 4. Log out and log in as the new account.
column4: The account is created with role TRAINER_LEAD; login with the set credentials succeeds and lands on the Course Manager dashboard.
column5: Admin logged in; a fresh email available.

Account- Role & Access Administration Fl: Admin attempts to create an account with an invalid/typo role string and it is rejected.
column3: 1. On Create Account, attempt to submit a role value that isn't LEARNER/TRAINER/TRAINER_LEAD/ADMINISTRATOR (e.g. via a manipulated request if the UI dropdown itself prevents typing free text).
column4: Creation is rejected (`IllegalArgumentException`-backed error); no account is created and no garbage `Role` row is added to the `roles` table for the typo'd value.
column15: Regression check - role whitelist fixed 2026-07-22; previously any non-empty string silently created a new Role row.

Account- Role & Access Administration Fl: Admin deactivates then reactivates a user account, and the login effect matches immediately.
column3: 1. Open a test user's detail. 2. Toggle status to INACTIVE and save. 3. Attempt login as that user (expect blocked, cross-ref SYS_FLOW_AUTH_TC08). 4. Toggle status back to ACTIVE and retry login.
column4: While INACTIVE, login is blocked; once reactivated to ACTIVE, login succeeds again immediately.

Account- Role & Access Administration Fl: Admin cannot deactivate their own account via the dedicated status endpoint.
column3: 1. Log in as ADMINISTRATOR. 2. Open your own account detail. 3. Attempt to set your own status to INACTIVE and save.
column4: The action is rejected with a self-lock protection message; the Admin's own status remains ACTIVE and they stay logged in.
column5: Logged in as the Administrator whose own account is being targeted.

Account- Role & Access Administration Fl: Admin cannot deactivate their own account via the combined Update Account screen either.
column3: 1. Open your own account detail's full "Update Account" edit form (not just the quick status toggle). 2. Change the status field to INACTIVE as part of a broader edit and save.
column4: The same self-lock protection blocks this path too; the Admin's own status stays ACTIVE.
column5: Logged in as the Administrator whose own account is being targeted.
column15: Regression check - `PUT /api/admin/users/{id}` previously lacked this check entirely (fixed 2026-07-22), unlike `PUT /api/admin/users/{id}/status` which always had it.

Account- Role & Access Administration Fl: Setting a user's status to an arbitrary non-whitelisted string via Update Account is rejected.
column3: 1. Open a test user's Update Account form. 2. Attempt to set status to a value outside ACTIVE/INACTIVE (e.g. "BANNED") and save.
column4: The save is rejected by the same status whitelist enforced on the dedicated status endpoint; the user's actual stored status is unchanged.
column15: Regression check - `PUT /api/admin/users/{id}` previously called `setStatus(...)` with zero validation, bypassing both the whitelist and the self-lock check (fixed 2026-07-22).

Account- Role & Access Administration Fl: Updating a user's role to an unknown role string via Update Account is rejected.
column3: 1. Open a test user's Update Account form. 2. Attempt to set role to a string that is not an existing Role (e.g. "SUPERADMIN") and save.
column4: The save is rejected with a "Role not found" style error; the user's existing role is unchanged.
column15: Note the intentional asymmetry vs Create Account (TC06): update rejects unknown roles as 'not found' since every valid role already exists as a row, while create explains the whitelist instead.

Account- Role & Access Administration Fl: The Audit Log records the account actions just performed by this Admin.
column3: 1. Immediately after TC05/TC07, open Admin > Audit Log.
column4: Entries appear for the account-creation (TC05) and status-change (TC07) actions, showing who performed them, on which user, and when.
column5: TC05 and TC07 were just performed.

Account- Role & Access Administration Fl: The Audit Log does not record actions taken outside AdminController's scope.
column3: 1. Have a Course Manager publish/reject a course (SYS_FLOW_CRS_TC15/16) and settle a statement (SYS_FLOW_REV_TC10). 2. Reopen the Audit Log.
column4: Neither the course review action nor the statement settlement appears in this Audit Log - it is scoped strictly to create/update-profile/role/status/activate-deactivate actions taken through AdminController, by design.
column5: A Course review action and a statement settlement have just occurred elsewhere.
column15: Confirms the documented scope limitation in doc/specs/03-rbac.md - not a bug to report, just verify it matches.

Account- Role & Access Administration Fl: AI Usage stats reflect real call activity, increasing after Learner AI Assistant/Recommendation usage.
column3: 1. Note the Total AI Calls figure. 2. Have a Learner send several AI Assistant chat messages (SYS_FLOW_AIR_TC01-TC05). 3. Reopen AI Usage stats.
column4: Total AI Calls increases by the number of new calls made; the chat-vs-embedding split and success rate update accordingly.
column5: Admin logged in; ability to compare before/after AI Usage figures.

Account- Role & Access Administration Fl: A non-Administrator cannot reach any /api/admin/** screen or action.
column3: 1. Log in as TRAINER_LEAD (or TRAINER/LEARNER). 2. Attempt to navigate to Admin Dashboard/Accounts/Audit Log/AI Usage directly.
column4: Navigation is blocked/hidden for non-ADMINISTRATOR roles; any direct API call returns 403 Forbidden (`@PreAuthorize(\hasRole('ADMINISTRATOR')\")` on every AdminController endpoint) - note that the required authority is the literal string ADMINISTRATOR

Account- Role & Access Administration Fl: The static Roles tab's descriptions match what each role can actually do in the running system.
column3: 1. Open Admin > Roles tab. 2. Read the LEARNER/TRAINER/TRAINER_LEAD/ADMINISTRATOR cards. 3. Spot-check at least one claim per role against actual observed behavior from other flows (e.g. TRAINER_LEAD can publish courses per SYS_FLOW_CRS, but cannot see revenue on the Admin dashboard per SYS_FLOW_REV_TC13).
column4: Every spot-checked claim on the Roles tab matches real enforced behavior seen elsewhere in this test plan - none of it is aspirational/marketing copy no longer true of the code.
column5: Admin logged in; results from SYS_FLOW_CRS/SYS_FLOW_REV available for comparison.
